newsitem.title: UK: UK radio advertising revenues top 300 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK radio advertising revenues top 300 mln stg.

text.p: Radio advertising revenues in Britain increased 10 percent in the 1996 third quarter, pushing revenues for the 12 months ended September to 300 million pounds, the Radio Advertising Bureau said on Friday.
It is the first time that British commercial radio advertising revenues for a one-year period have reached the 300 million pound mark, the trade group said.

"In the year to September the advertising industry invested just over 300 million pounds on commercial radio, a year-on-year increase of the order of 15 percent," Justin Sampson, operations manager of the RAB told a news conference.

Third-quarter radio advertising revenue totalled 77 million pounds, up just over 10 percent from the prior-year quarter. The quarterly growth rate was below the growth rate posted earlier in the year.
In the 1996 first quarter radio advertising revenues grew 20 percent on a year-over-year basis, followed by an increase of 18.5 percent in the second quarter.

Radio, however, continues to command a growing share of Britain's total display advertising market, reaching 4.5 percent for the year to June 1996. Radio in the 1996 first quarter had posted a 4.3 percent market share.
Radio advertising is expected to be close to a five percent market share by year-end.

"It appears likely that the steady slowdown that was seen in advertising expenditure growth until the second quarter of '96 has been resumed," Sampson said, citing preliminary analysis of advertising figures. "Our initial estimate is that it looks as though commercial radio growth will be twice that of the overall display marketplace, while it looks as though television advertising revenue increased by only 0.3 percent in the third quarter."

"From this standpoint we are optimistic that we will be able to report further share growth for commercial radio in three months time and that the year-end figure for 1996 will continue to close on five percent," Sampson said.
